sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九的隐形世界。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: This is the American dream of freedom on wheels.
sentences.zh: 这是美国人对轮子上自由的梦想。

sentences.en: An automotive age, traveling on time-saving superhighways.
sentences.zh: 这是一个汽车时代，行驶在节省时间的高速公路上。

sentences.en: The 1940s, 50s, and 60s were the golden age of road travel.
sentences.zh: 20世纪40、50和60年代是公路旅行的黄金时代。

sentences.en: Cars had become cheap and roomy enough to carry families comfortably for hundreds of miles.
sentences.zh: 汽车变得便宜且宽敞，足以让家庭舒适地出行数百英里。

sentences.en: The interstate highway system had started to connect the country's smaller roads into a vast nationwide network.
sentences.zh: 州际高速公路系统开始将全国较小的道路连接成一个庞大的全国网络。

sentences.en: Finally, tourists could make their way from New York to California,
sentences.zh: 终于，游客们可以从纽约前往加利福尼亚，

sentences.en: with the windows down and the wind in their hair, seeing the grandeur of America along the way.
sentences.zh: 摇下车窗，微风拂面，沿途欣赏美国的壮丽风光。

sentences.en: We have become the nation on wheels, with more motorized mobility than ever dreamed of before.
sentences.zh: 我们已经成为了一个车轮上的国家，拥有前所未有的机动出行能力。

sentences.en: But, of course, this freedom and mobility wasn't available to everyone.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，这种自由和机动性并非人人都能享有。

sentences.en: That's our brand new producer and splash of cold water, Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的全新制作人兼一盆冷水，德兰妮·霍尔。

sentences.en: Because in 1956, the year that federal funding made the interstate highway system possible,
sentences.zh: 因为在1956年，也就是联邦资金使州际高速公路系统成为现实的那一年，

sentences.en: Jim Crow was still the law of the land.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·克劳法仍然是国家的法律。

sentences.en: In the South, racial segregation was enforced by law,
sentences.zh: 在南方，种族隔离是通过法律强制执行的，

sentences.en: and had been since shortly after Reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 而且自重建时期结束后不久就一直是这样。

sentences.en: In many parts of the North, the codes were enforced in practice.
sentences.zh: 在北方的许多地方，这些法规在实践中得到执行。

sentences.en: And these codes could make a simple road trip really complicated for black travelers.
sentences.zh: 而这些法规会让黑人旅客的一次简单公路旅行变得非常复杂。

sentences.en: How is this?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Is that a good level?
sentences.zh: 这个音量可以吗？

sentences.en: Are you picking me up well there?
sentences.zh: 你听我这里声音清楚吗？

sentences.en: This is Curtis Graves.
sentences.zh: 这是柯蒂斯·格雷夫斯。

sentences.en: Okay, my name is Curtis Graves, and I was born in 1938,
sentences.zh: 好的，我叫柯蒂斯·格雷夫斯，我出生于1938年，

sentences.en: so I'm a little older than most of the people who are listening to this.
sentences.zh: 所以我比听这个节目的大多数人都年长一些。

sentences.en: Curtis would eventually become a Texas state representative,
sentences.zh: 柯蒂斯后来成为了一名德克萨斯州众议员，

sentences.en: and then he'd go on to work at NASA, and then he'd become a photographer.
sentences.zh: 然后他去美国宇航局工作，接着又成为了一名摄影师。

sentences.en: But as a kid, he grew up in the segregated South.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个孩子，他在实行种族隔离的南方长大。

sentences.en: And for many years, his parents tried to shield him from that reality.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他的父母一直试图向他隐瞒那个现实。

sentences.en: I've often said that both my mother and father were the best liars that I knew.
sentences.zh: 我经常说，我的母亲和父亲是我认识的最好的说谎者。

sentences.en: For instance, we sat in the back of the bus because it was cooler there.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们坐在公车后排，因为那里更凉快。

sentences.en: We rode in the front of the train because you could get off quicker.
sentences.zh: 我们坐火车的头等车厢，因为那样可以更快下车。

sentences.en: We sat upstairs in the movie because you had better seats than the upstairs.
sentences.zh: 我们在电影院坐楼上，因为楼上的座位更好。

sentences.en: Of course, that ruse couldn't laSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，这种把戏无法持久。

sentences.en: And by the time Curtis was a college senior in Houston, Texas, in the mid-1950s,
sentences.zh: 到20世纪50年代中期柯蒂斯在德克萨斯州休斯顿读大学四年级时，

sentences.en: he was fully aware of what it meant to be a black person living under Jim Crow.
sentences.zh: 他已经完全意识到了生活在吉姆·克劳法之下的黑人意味着什么。

sentences.en: There's one experience in particular that stands out in his mind.
sentences.zh: 有一段经历在他脑海中尤为深刻。

sentences.en: He was just 21 years old and getting ready to drive to a college meeting in Waco,
sentences.zh: 他当时年仅21岁，准备开车去韦科参加一个大学会议，

sentences.en: about three hours northwest of Houston.
sentences.zh: 那是位于休斯顿西北约三小时车程的地方。

sentences.en: He'd agreed to take a couple of acquaintances.
sentences.zh: 他答应带几个熟人一起去。

sentences.en: They happened to be white women.
sentences.zh: 他们碰巧是白人女性。

sentences.en: I said to myself, I might be in for some difficult times here,
sentences.zh: 我对自己说，我在这里可能会遇到一些困难，

sentences.en: but, you know, I had to soldier on.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我必须硬着头皮坚持下去。

sentences.en: To get to Waco, Curtis had to drive through a stretch of East Texas
sentences.zh: 为了到达韦科，柯蒂斯不得不穿过德克萨斯州东部的一段路，

sentences.en: that was notorious in those decades for racial violence.
sentences.zh: 那里的地区在那些年代以种族暴力而闻名。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Those communities were pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 那些社区相当糟糕。

sentences.en: Around dusk, the travelers got hungry, so they pulled over at a roadside diner.
sentences.zh: 黄昏时分，旅行者们饿了，于是他们在一家路边餐馆停下车。

sentences.en: As soon as we got in the front door, the guy said,
sentences.zh: 我们一进前门，那家伙就说，

sentences.en: Ah, I'm sorry, but you can't come in here.
sentences.zh: 啊，我很抱歉，但你们不能进这里。

sentences.en: We don't serve black people at all.
sentences.zh: 我们根本不接待黑人。

sentences.en: So the three of them went back outside, and Curtis devised a plan.
sentences.zh: 于是他们三个人又回到了外面，柯蒂斯想出了一个计划。

sentences.en: They'd try another restaurant right across the street.
sentences.zh: 他们去试试街对面的另一家餐馆。

sentences.en: I said to them, the two of you go in, get a table,
sentences.zh: 我对他们说，你们两个进去，找一张桌子，

sentences.en: and after you're seated and the waiter or waitress comes up to you,
sentences.zh: 等你们坐下后，服务员过来时，

sentences.en: tell them that you have a boy that's driving you
sentences.zh: 告诉他们你们有一个负责开车的男孩，

sentences.en: and that you want to know whether you can bring him in to eat.
sentences.zh: 并问他们是否可以带他进来吃饭。

sentences.en: So the women walked inside,
sentences.zh: 于是女士们走进餐厅，

sentences.en: and they asked the waitress if Curtis could come inside to join them.
sentences.zh: 她们问服务员柯蒂斯是否可以进来加入她们。

sentences.en: And the lady said, of course, no problem at all.
sentences.zh: 那位女士说，当然可以，完全没问题。

sentences.en: So as long as I was their boy and their driver,
sentences.zh: 所以，只要我是他们的男孩和司机，

sentences.en: I could eat with them at a table in a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 我就能和他们在餐馆里同桌吃饭。

sentences.en: But if I were equal to them, I could not.
sentences.zh: 但如果我和他们平等，我就不能。

sentences.en: This kind of humiliation on the road was routine
sentences.zh: 这种在路上的羞辱是家常便饭，

sentences.en: and had been going on for decades.
sentences.zh: 而且已经持续了几十年。

sentences.en: Many people wrote in to the NAACP around this time,
sentences.zh: 大约在这个时候，许多人写信给全国有色人种协进会，

sentences.en: describing experiences just like Curtis's.
sentences.zh: 描述了和柯蒂斯一模一样的经历。

sentences.en: To whom it may concern,
sentences.zh: 尊敬的负责人：

sentences.en: before starting our recent vacation trip to several eastern states...
sentences.zh: 在我们开始最近前往几个东部州的度假旅行之前……

sentences.en: Dear sir, I am a member of the NAACP,
sentences.zh: 亲爱的先生，我是全国有色人种协进会的会员，

sentences.en: and in a court...
sentences.zh: 在法庭上……

sentences.en: I would like to report an incident occurring on January 1st
sentences.zh: 我想报告一起发生在1月1日的事件，

sentences.en: at a golf service station in Macon, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 地点在佐治亚州梅肯的一个海湾加油站。

sentences.en: My wife and I went to the restrooms to refresh ourselves,
sentences.zh: 我和妻子去洗手间洗漱，

sentences.en: then found a vacant table.
sentences.zh: 然后发现了一张空桌子。

sentences.en: Ten minutes passed, and no one came to service.
sentences.zh: 十分钟过去了，没有人来服务。

sentences.en: He informed me that the restroom for the colored was in the back.
sentences.zh: 他通知我，有色人种专用洗手间在后面。

sentences.en: It seems to me dealers should not be permitted to sell gas and oil
sentences.zh: 在我看来，经销商不应该被允许出售汽油和机油，

sentences.en: and not provide these comforts for us also.
sentences.zh: 却不为我们提供这些便利设施。

sentences.en: Some travelers would drive all night
sentences.zh: 一些旅客会开车一整夜，

sentences.en: instead of trying to find lodging in an unfamiliar and possibly dangerous town.
sentences.zh: 也不愿在一个陌生且可能危险的城镇寻找住宿。

sentences.en: They'd pack picnics so they didn't have to stop for food.
sentences.zh: 他们会打包野餐食品，这样就不用停下来买吃的。

sentences.en: Some people would even carry portable toilets in the trunks of their cars,
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至会在汽车后备箱里携带便携式马桶，

sentences.en: knowing that there was a good chance they'd be turned away from roadside restrooMs.
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道自己极有可能会被路边洗手间拒绝进入。

sentences.en: But since 1936, a guy named Victor Hugo Green
sentences.zh: 但自1936年以来，一个名叫维克托·雨果·格林的人

sentences.en: had been trying to help with some of these problems
sentences.zh: 一直试图帮助解决其中一些问题，

sentences.en: to make life easier for thousands of black motorists.
sentences.zh: 为成千上万的黑人驾车者让生活更轻松。

sentences.en: State by state, he'd been putting together a travel guide
sentences.zh: 他逐个州地汇编了一本旅行指南，

sentences.en: with listings of restaurants, hotels, and service stations
sentences.zh: 里面列出了欢迎非裔美国旅客的餐厅、酒店和加油站。

sentences.en: that would welcome African American travelers.
sentences.zh: 他将其命名为《黑人汽车司机绿皮书》。

sentences.en: He called it the Negro Motorist Green Book.
sentences.zh: 简称《绿皮书》。

sentences.en: The Green Book for short.
sentences.zh: 简称《绿皮书》。

sentences.en: Victor Green, who died in 1960,
sentences.zh: 维克托·格林于1960年逝世，

sentences.en: lived in Harlem, New York during the height of the Harlem Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 在哈莱姆文艺复兴鼎盛时期，他住在纽约哈莱姆。

sentences.en: His apartment was not far from Duke Ellington's.
sentences.zh: 他的公寓离杜克·艾灵顿的住所不远。

sentences.en: His office would eventually be situated near Smalls Paradise,
sentences.zh: 他的办公室后来设在斯莫尔天堂附近，

sentences.en: a famous nightclub.
sentences.zh: 那是一家著名的夜总会。

sentences.en: Victor didn't have the most obvious background for starting a travel guide.
sentences.zh: 维克托的背景并不是编写旅行指南最显眼的人选。

sentences.en: He didn't work in tourism.
sentences.zh: 他没有从事旅游业。

sentences.en: He wasn't a writer.
sentences.zh: 他不是作家。

sentences.en: He was a mailman in Hackensack, New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 他是新泽西州哈肯萨克的邮递员。

sentences.en: But he kept hearing stories about discrimination on the road.
sentences.zh: 但他不断听到关于路上遭遇歧视的故事。

sentences.en: So he would go do his route in Hackensack, New Jersey,
sentences.zh: 因此他会在新泽西州哈肯萨克送信，

sentences.en: come back home and work on the Green Book at night,
sentences.zh: 回到家后在夜里编写《绿皮书》，

sentences.en: compiling these addresses, typing them up,
sentences.zh: 收集这些地址，把它们打字录入，

sentences.en: and putting them in their book form.
sentences.zh: 并将它们整理成书面形式。

sentences.en: This is Calvin Alexander Ramsey.
sentences.zh: 这是卡尔文·亚历山大·拉姆齐。
zh_words: 卡尔文·亚历山大·拉姆齐

sentences.en: Playwright, author, and filmmaker.
sentences.zh: 剧作家、作家兼电影制作人。

sentences.en: And years ago, Calvin started researching the history of the Green Book.
sentences.zh: 几年前，卡尔文开始研究《绿皮书》的历史。

sentences.en: He learned that the Green Book wasn't really the first guide of its kind.
sentences.zh: 他了解到，《绿皮书》其实并不是同类指南中的第一本。

sentences.en: In fact, Victor may have gotten the idea from Jewish travelers.
sentences.zh: 事实上，维克托的想法可能是从犹太旅客那里得到的。

sentences.en: Because the Jewish community was also having issues on the open road,
sentences.zh: 因为犹太社群在公开道路上也遇到了问题，

sentences.en: with a lot of the places saying restricted,
sentences.zh: 许多地方挂着“受限制”的牌子，

sentences.en: and that was a code word for Gentiles only.
sentences.zh: 那是仅限非犹太人进入的代名词。

sentences.en: When Victor published his first Green Book, it just covered New York.
sentences.zh: 当维克托出版他的第一本《绿皮书》时，它只涵盖了纽约。

sentences.en: And he heard from around the country from other carriers and other people saying,
sentences.zh: 他听到全国各地的其他运输业者和其他人说，

sentences.en: we really need this nationwide.
sentences.zh: 我们真的在全国范围内需要这个。

sentences.en: But it wasn't that easy to gather information from across the country back then.
sentences.zh: 但当时要从全国各地收集信息并非易事。

sentences.en: Long-distance phone calls were expensive.
sentences.zh: 长途电话很昂贵。

sentences.en: And that, Calvin says, is when Victor Green realized
sentences.zh: 卡尔文说，正是在那个时候，维克托·格林意识到

sentences.en: that being a mailman was his secret superpower.
sentences.zh: 身为邮递员是他的秘密超能力。

sentences.en: There were African-American letter carriers all over the United States at this time.
sentences.zh: 那时全美国到处都是非裔美国邮递员。

sentences.en: We're talking about 1936.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是1936年。

sentences.en: And so he knew about, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以他了解，你知道的，

sentences.en: the relationships that the mailmen have with their homeowners
sentences.zh: 邮递员在投递信件时与房主或公寓居民建立的关系。

sentences.en: or apartment dwellers delivering their mail.
sentences.zh: 或公寓居民递送邮件。

sentences.en: So just like today, the mailman is part of the community.
sentences.zh: 所以就像今天一样，邮递员是社区的一部分。

sentences.en: So Calvin says Victor tapped into this network,
sentences.zh: 因此卡尔文说，维克托利用了这个网络，

sentences.en: spreading the word about his guide through the National Alliance of Postal and Federal Employees,
sentences.zh: 通过全国邮政和联邦雇员联盟（一个邮递员工会）宣传他的指南。

sentences.en: a letter carrier union.
sentences.zh: 一个邮递员工会。

sentences.en: Calvin says postal workers across the country
sentences.zh: 卡尔文说，全国各地的邮政工人

sentences.en: scouted potential Green Book locations in their cities and towns.
sentences.zh: 在各自的城市和城镇物色潜在的《绿皮书》收录地点。

sentences.en: He says some even asked families they delivered to
sentences.zh: 他说有些人甚至询问他们投递信件的家庭，

sentences.en: if they'd be open to hosting travelers in their homes.
sentences.zh: 是否愿意在家里接待旅客。

sentences.en: And if they agreed, then they would send the information to Victor Green in Harlem.
sentences.zh: 如果他们同意，就会把信息发送给在哈莱姆的维克托·格林。

sentences.en: Victor was able to get a field force of letter carriers who were all over the country
sentences.zh: 维克托能够拥有一支遍布全国的邮递员外勤队伍，

sentences.en: who acquired materials and names and addresses and businesses for him.
sentences.zh: 他们为他获取了材料、名字、地址和商业机构信息。

sentences.en: Wherever there was a black mailman, you had a Green Book salesman or recruiter.
sentences.zh: 只要有黑人邮递员的地方，就会有一个《绿皮书》的推销员或招募员。

sentences.en: Pretty quickly, the Green Book caught on.
sentences.zh: 很快，《绿皮书》就流行起来了。

sentences.en: Businesses, many black-owned, began getting in touch with Victor,
sentences.zh: 许多黑人拥有的企业开始与维克托联系，

sentences.en: hoping to advertise and hoping to be listed.
sentences.zh: 希望能做广告并被收录其中。

sentences.en: Black newspapers signed on as sponsors.
sentences.zh: 黑人报纸也签约成为赞助商。

sentences.en: Victor eventually retired from his job as a letter carrier
sentences.zh: 维克托最终从邮递员的岗位上退休，

sentences.en: and started working on the guide full-time.
sentences.zh: 开始全职从事指南的工作。

sentences.en: He even opened an affiliated travel agency that helped tourists arrange trips.
sentences.zh: 他甚至开设了一家附属旅行社，帮助游客安排行程。

sentences.en: But still, there was the challenge of distribution.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，分发仍然是一个挑战。

sentences.en: How to get the guide into the hands of travelers who needed it.
sentences.zh: 如何将指南送到需要它的旅行者手中。

sentences.en: That happened in a few ways.
sentences.zh: 这通过几种途径实现。

sentences.en: The United States Travel Bureau signed on to help out.
sentences.zh: 美国旅游局签约提供帮助。

sentences.en: And then there were the more informal networks.
sentences.zh: 还有那些更非正式的网络。

sentences.en: Well, churches, Pullman Porters, the Urban League, the NAACP, the Masonic Lodges.
sentences.zh: 嗯，教堂、普尔曼列车员、城市联盟、全国有色人种协进会、共济会会所。

sentences.en: There was a very wide, varied distribution process in place for these Green Books.
sentences.zh: 这些《绿皮书》在当时有着非常广泛且多样的发行渠道。

sentences.en: And there was an important corporate sponsor, too.
sentences.zh: 而且，还有一个重要的企业赞助商。

sentences.en: A big one.
sentences.zh: 一个大金主。

sentences.en: For service that is tops, and gas that's extra fine.
sentences.zh: 服务顶呱呱，汽油特优质。

sentences.en: There's a smile for every mile at the ESSO sign.
sentences.zh: 埃索标志下，英里绽笑颜。

sentences.en: E-S-S-O makes your car go.
sentences.zh: 埃索让您的汽车飞驰。

sentences.en: Happy motoring.
sentences.zh: 祝您一路平安。

sentences.en: ESSO, also known as Standard Oil and now known as ExxonMobil,
sentences.zh: 埃索，也就是标准石油，现在名为埃克森美孚，

sentences.en: was one of the few oil companies back then that actively pursued black customers.
sentences.zh: 是当时极少数积极争取黑人客户的石油公司之一。

sentences.en: They franchised their stations to African-American operators.
sentences.zh: 他们将加油站特许经营权授予非洲裔美国人运营商。

sentences.en: And they had a black representative on staff, James Billboard Jackson,
sentences.zh: 他们的员工中还有一位黑人代表，詹姆斯·比尔博德·杰克逊，
zh_words: 詹姆斯·比尔博德·杰克逊

sentences.en: who helped place Green Books in many of those stations, as well as the white-owned ones.
sentences.zh: 他协助将《绿皮书》投放到许多这类加油站，以及白人拥有的加油站中。

sentences.en: ESSO may have done this out of a sense of fairness and equality.
sentences.zh: 埃索这样做可能是出于公平和平等的意识。

sentences.en: John D.
sentences.zh: 约翰·D·

sentences.en: Rockefeller, who founded Standard Oil in 1870, had married into a family of abolitionists
sentences.zh: 洛克菲勒在1870年创立了标准石油，他与一个废奴主义者家族联姻，

sentences.en: who were part of the Underground Railroad, and he'd voted for Abraham Lincoln back in the day.
sentences.zh: 该家族曾是“地下铁路”的一部分，他当年还曾投票给亚伯拉罕·林肯。

sentences.en: But ESSO probably did it for another reason, too.
sentences.zh: 但埃索这样做的原因可能还有另一个。

sentences.en: Money, honey.
sentences.zh: 钱，宝贝。

sentences.en: It has to do with money.
sentences.zh: 这与钱有关。

sentences.en: Remember Curtis, who had the crappy experience driving across East Texas?
sentences.zh: 还记得柯蒂斯吗？他曾在德克萨斯州东部有过糟糕的驾车经历。

sentences.en: His dad operated one of the first black-owned ESSO stations in New Orleans,
sentences.zh: 他的父亲经营着新奥尔良最早的黑人拥有的埃索加油站之一，

sentences.en: where Curtis was born and raised.
sentences.zh: 柯蒂斯正是在那里出生并长大的。

sentences.en: It was called Bootsy and Buddies.
sentences.zh: 它叫“布蒂与巴迪”。

sentences.en: The economic logic of stocking the Green Book was pretty simple, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，销售《绿皮书》的商业逻辑其实很简单。

sentences.en: If you want black people to buy your fuel,
sentences.zh: 如果你想让黑人购买你的燃油，

sentences.en: why don't you give them an opportunity to see that they can travel
sentences.zh: 为什么不给他们一个机会，让他们看到自己也可以去旅行，

sentences.en: and find places to stay while they're on the road traveling?
sentences.zh: 并且能在上路旅行时找到住宿的地方呢？

sentences.en: So Curtis's dad kept a shelf of Green Books for his customers.
sentences.zh: 因此，柯蒂斯的父亲为他的顾客准备了一个摆放《绿皮书》的书架。

sentences.en: You know, somebody came in and said,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有人走进来，然后说：

sentences.en: Buddy, I'm thinking about taking a trip to Chicago.
sentences.zh: “巴迪，我正考虑去芝加哥一趟。”

sentences.en: My dad would say,
sentences.zh: 我父亲就会说：

sentences.en: Well, do you know where to stop between here and Chicago?
sentences.zh: “好吧，你知道从这儿到芝加哥之间该在哪儿落脚吗？”

sentences.en: And the person would say,
sentences.zh: 那人就会回答：

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: “不知道。”

sentences.en: He'd say,
sentences.zh: 他会说：

sentences.en: Well, here.
sentences.zh: “好吧，给你。”

sentences.en: The Green Book will tell you.
sentences.zh: “《绿皮书》会告诉你。”

sentences.en: And it gave you a sense of security.
sentences.zh: 这给你带来了一种安全感。

sentences.en: And so the Green Book came to cover listings in all 50 states
sentences.zh: 因此，《绿皮书》最终涵盖了全美所有50个州的指南，

sentences.en: and even some locations in Canada, the Caribbean, and Mexico.
sentences.zh: 甚至还包括加拿大、加勒比地区和墨西哥的一些地点。

sentences.en: They printed about 15,000 copies a year.
sentences.zh: 他们每年印制大约15,000册。

sentences.en: Victor Green had changed travel for thousands of African-American tourists.
sentences.zh: 维克托·格林改变了成千上万非洲裔美国游客的旅行方式。

sentences.en: He wrote in a 1956 introduction to the guide.
sentences.zh: 他在1956年为该指南写的序言中这样写道。

sentences.en: Now, things are different.
sentences.zh: 如今，情况不同了。

sentences.en: The Negro traveler can depend on the Green Book for all the information he wants.
sentences.zh: 黑人旅行者可以依靠《绿皮书》获取他所需的所有信息。

sentences.en: This guide has made traveling more popular without encountering embarrassing situations.
sentences.zh: 这本指南让旅行变得更受欢迎，而不会遭遇尴尬的处境。

sentences.en: But as the civil rights struggle continued,
sentences.zh: 但随着民权斗争的继续，

sentences.en: some people began to question the value of the Green Book.
sentences.zh: 一些人开始质疑《绿皮书》的价值。

sentences.en: Black people, many of them, began to feel that this was accommodating to Jim Crow.
sentences.zh: 许多黑人开始觉得，这是在对吉姆·克劳法妥协。

sentences.en: Susan Roo is a professor of history at Brigham Young University.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·鲁是杨百翰大学的历史学教授。

sentences.en: And she says that the Green Book began to seem a little out of step with the times.
sentences.zh: 她表示，《绿皮书》开始显得有点与时代脱节。

sentences.en: It rarely took on an overtly political tone, especially in its early days.
sentences.zh: 它很少带有公开的政治色彩，特别是在其早期。

sentences.en: And there were actually other Black travel guides published around the same time that did.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大约在同一时期出版的其他黑人旅行指南却带有这种色彩。

sentences.en: One called Travel Guide, for instance.
sentences.zh: 比如其中一本叫《旅行指南》的刊物。

sentences.en: Travel Guide listed where the NAACP chapters were in each city.
sentences.zh: 《旅行指南》列出了每个城市全国有色人种协进会（NAACP）分部的位置。

sentences.en: They were much more attuned with civil rights.
sentences.zh: 它们更加契合民权运动。

sentences.en: Much more political tone.
sentences.zh: 政治色彩浓厚得多。

sentences.en: Eventually, the NAACP made it clear.
sentences.zh: 最终，全国有色人种协进会表明了立场。

sentences.en: And the NAACP said,
sentences.zh: 全国有色人种协进会表示：

sentences.en: what we're striving for, we're striving for integration.
sentences.zh: “我们所争取的目标，是我们所追求的融合。”

sentences.en: And so that's their stand.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的立场。

sentences.en: And the NAACP built a lot of their push for the 1964 Civil Rights Act,
sentences.zh: 而且，全国有色人种协进会为其推动1964年《民权法案》奠定了大量基础，

sentences.en: which outlawed discrimination based on race,
sentences.zh: 该法案宣布基于种族的歧视违法，

sentences.en: and ended Jim Crow around this idea of total integration.
sentences.zh: 并以全面融合的理念终结了吉姆·克劳法。

sentences.en: In fact, when the NAACP testified during the debate over the bill,
sentences.zh: 事实上，当全国有色人种协进会在有关该法案的辩论中作证时，

sentences.en: they drew on all those letters they'd received about discrimination on the road.
sentences.zh: 他们利用了收到的所有关于途中遭遇歧视的信件。

sentences.en: They appealed to that vision of the iconic family road trip,
sentences.zh: 他们呼吁人们对标志性的家庭公路旅行、

sentences.en: of the freedom to explore America by car.
sentences.zh: 以及开车探索美国的自由产生向往。

sentences.en: Roy Wilkins, the executive secretary of the NAACP,
sentences.zh: 全国有色人种协进会执行秘书罗伊·威尔金斯，

sentences.en: spoke before the Senate's Commerce Committee in 1963.
sentences.zh: 于1963年在参议院商业委员会前发表了讲话。

sentences.en: As soon as Congress gets out,
sentences.zh: 国会一旦休会，

sentences.en: they're all going to head into their station wagons and go back to their home district.
sentences.zh: 他们全都会钻进旅行车，返回各自的选区。

sentences.en: It's July in Washington.
sentences.zh: 那是七月的华盛顿。

sentences.en: It's really hot.
sentences.zh: 天气非常热。

sentences.en: Wilkins asked the Senate to imagine
sentences.zh: 威尔金斯请参议院想象一下，

sentences.en: what it might be like to travel as a black person.
sentences.zh: 作为一个黑人去旅行会是什么样的体验。

sentences.en: Would you like me to read what Roy Wilkins said?
sentences.zh: 需要我读一下罗伊·威尔金斯说过的话吗？

sentences.en: How far do you drive each day?
sentences.zh: 你每天开多远的车？

sentences.en: Where and under what conditions can you and your family eat?
sentences.zh: 你和你的家人可以在哪里、在什么条件下吃饭？

sentences.en: Where can they use a restroom?
sentences.zh: 他们可以在哪里上厕所？

sentences.en: Can you stop driving after a reasonable day behind the wheel?
sentences.zh: 你在方向盘后度过合理的一天后，能停下来不开了吗？

sentences.en: Or must you drive until you reach a city
sentences.zh: 还是说你必须一直开到某个城市，

sentences.en: where relatives or friends will accommodate you and yours for the night?
sentences.zh: 在那里亲戚或朋友能为你和你的家人提供当晚的住宿？

sentences.en: Will your children be denied a soft drink
sentences.zh: 你的孩子会因为他们不是白人而被拒绝提供汽水

sentences.en: or an ice cream cone because they are not white?
sentences.zh: 或冰淇淋甜筒吗？

sentences.en: So he's appealing to them at the most basic level of their own love for their own family.
sentences.zh: 因此，他是在从他们对自身家庭最基本的爱这一层面去打动他们。

sentences.en: And Susan thinks this may have been one of the things that helped pass the bill.
sentences.zh: 苏珊认为，这可能是帮助该法案通过的原因之一。

sentences.en: By framing the narrative of civil rights as a family travel narrative,
sentences.zh: 通过将民权叙事构建为一个家庭旅行叙事，

sentences.en: they were able to convince the senators to vote for the bill.
sentences.zh: 他们得以说服参议员们投票赞成该法案。

sentences.en: In 1964, President Lyndon Johnson signed the bill into law.
sentences.zh: 1964年，林登·约翰逊总统将该法案签署成为法律。

sentences.en: Congress passes the most sweeping civil rights bill ever to be written into the law
sentences.zh: 国会通过了有史以来最广泛的民权法案并将其写进法律，

sentences.en: and thus reaffirms the conception of equality for all men
sentences.zh: 从而重申了人人平等的观念，

sentences.en: that began with Lincoln and the Civil War 100 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这一观念始于100年前的林肯和南北战争。

sentences.en: The Negro won his freedom then.
sentences.zh: 黑人那时赢得了自由。

sentences.en: He wins his dignity now.
sentences.zh: 他现在赢得了尊严。

sentences.en: The civil rights struggle was not over then and it's still not over today.
sentences.zh: 民权斗争在当时并未结束，直到今天也尚未结束。

sentences.en: But for Victor Green, it became clear at some point that his Green Book had a limited shelf life.
sentences.zh: 但对于维克托·格林来说，他在某个时刻清楚地认识到，他的《绿皮书》有着有限的生命周期。

sentences.en: He wrote in the introduction to one of his guides.
sentences.zh: 他在自己其中一本指南的序言中写道。

sentences.en: There will be a day sometime in the near future when this guide will not have to be published.
sentences.zh: 在不久的将来，总有一天这本指南将不再需要出版。

sentences.en: That is when we as a race will have equal opportunities and privileges in the United States.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们作为一个种族将在美国获得平等机会和特权的时候。

sentences.en: And sure enough, two years after the Civil Rights Act passed,
sentences.zh: 果不其然，《民权法案》通过两年后，

sentences.en: the Green Book published its last edition.
sentences.zh: 《绿皮书》出版了它的最后一版。

sentences.en: So actually, could you just describe where we are?
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，你能描述一下我们现在在哪里吗？

sentences.en: We're at the public library downtown, the Central Branch in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 我们在市中心的公共图书馆，洛杉矶中央分馆。

sentences.en: And we're down in the bowels, four floors down underground in the history and genealogy department.
sentences.zh: 我们在深处，地下四层的历史和家谱部门。

sentences.en: And you have a stack of books there in front of you.
sentences.zh: 你面前有一叠书。

sentences.en: What are those?
sentences.zh: 那些是什么？

sentences.en: They are green books.
sentences.zh: 它们是《绿皮书》。

sentences.en: They're just little jewels.
sentences.zh: 它们简直是小小的无价之宝。

sentences.en: I mean, I just buzz with this kind of good energy that I just feel like, oh my God, they're actually here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我整个人都洋溢着这种美好的活力，让我觉得，天哪，它们真的在这里。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: Candacy Taylor is a photographer and a cultural documentarian.
sentences.zh: 坎达西·泰勒是一位摄影师兼文化纪录片制作人。

sentences.en: The guides she's holding are small, maybe eight inches by five inches.
sentences.zh: 她手里拿着的指南很小，大约八英寸乘五英寸。

sentences.en: They have green covers, each with a different destination featured.
sentences.zh: 它们有着绿色的封面，每一个封面都以不同的目的地为特色。

sentences.en: And there are pages and pages of listings inside.
sentences.zh: 里面有密密麻麻的目录页。

sentences.en: Let me see.
sentences.zh: 让我看看。

sentences.en: There were beauty parlors, barbershops, tailors, taverns.
sentences.zh: 这里有美发沙龙、理发店、裁缝店、小酒馆。

sentences.en: There were nightclubs.
sentences.zh: 还有夜总会。

sentences.en: It was really a social network.
sentences.zh: 它真的成了一个社交网络。

sentences.en: It was anything you might want to do in that town and the resources that were available to you.
sentences.zh: 涵盖了你可能想在那个小镇做的事以及你可以利用的资源。

sentences.en: Candacy has been traveling the country, documenting old Green Book locations from California to Oklahoma to New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 坎达西一直在全国各地旅行，记录从加利福尼亚到俄克拉荷马再到新墨西哥的旧《绿皮书》地点。

sentences.en: Many establishments are now run by people who don't know much, if anything, about the place's history.
sentences.zh: 许多场所现在由对这段历史知之甚少（甚至一无所知）的人经营。

sentences.en: Some of the buildings are gone, and what's left is just an empty lot or a patch of grass.
sentences.zh: 其中一些建筑已经消失，剩下的只是一片空地或一块草地。

sentences.en: Even these original copies of the guide are rare now.
sentences.zh: 现在连这些指南的原版也极为罕见。

sentences.en: The Smithsonian bought one at auction recently.
sentences.zh: 史密森尼学会最近在拍卖会上买了一本。

sentences.en: So look in your, if you're listening to this, and you know your parents, you know, lived during Jim Crow,
sentences.zh: 所以找找看，如果你正在听这个节目，而且你知道你的父母，你知道的，在吉姆·克劳法时期生活过，

sentences.en: look in your attics and see.
sentences.zh: 去你们的阁楼里找找看。

sentences.en: You might have a, you know, $20 plus thousand dollar guide.
sentences.zh: 你们可能藏着一本价值两万多美元的指南。

sentences.en: You never know.
sentences.zh: 你永远说不准。

sentences.en: $20,000 is a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 20,000美元是一笔巨款。

sentences.en: But back in 1936, when the Green Book first appeared and could be purchased for $0.25 by the travelers who needed it the most,
sentences.zh: 但在1936年，《绿皮书》首次问世时，最需要它的旅行者只需花0.25美元就能买到，

sentences.en: it was arguably worth even more.
sentences.zh: 可以说它甚至更有价值。

sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由德兰妮·霍尔制作，

sentences.zh: 要查找坎达西·泰勒拍摄的旧《绿皮书》地点的图片链接

sentences.zh: 我们是99%隐形公司的一个节目，这是旧金山KALW的一个项目，

sentences.zh: 制作地点位于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市美丽市中心的建筑与室内设计公司ArcSign的办公室。

sentences.zh: 如果你访问全新的99pi.org，你会发现新的非音频文章，

sentences.zh: 里面包含了所有你喜欢的99pi元素，而没有我啰啰嗦嗦的声音。

sentences.en: I'm really excited that we get to take on topics that are either too visual for the show
sentences.zh: 我真的很兴奋，我们能够涉足那些对节目来说视觉效果太强的话题，

sentences.zh: 但我也需要为此支付费用，所以我们正在尝试展示广告。

sentences.zh: 如果你能够动用一家酷炫且注重设计的公司的营销资金

sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并关注这个节目。
